correctness.rationale: For every a>0, b>=0, H>0, the normal two-dimensional flow reduces to two complex Cayley factors. Exact expansion yields F=(U-2c sqrt(R))/(U+2c sqrt(R)), monotone in U=w+(R+4 sigma^2)/w-4 sigma^2. Its strictly positive second derivative gives a unique clipped minimizer and all boundary/equality cases. The asymptotic limit follows from q~R^(-1/2); b=0 has exact midpoint zero. Actual verifier.py checks symbolic identities and performs 97,200 supplementary direct-complex tests; finite comparisons do not substitute for proof.

originality.rationale: The closest primary literature develops related numerical time integrators but optimizes different schemes/objectives. Zhang et al. 2020 general composite integrators use trapezoidal first stages and a general final stage, choosing parameters for accuracy/stability or low-frequency conservation. Their all-trapezoidal limiting case is not this fixed-budget complex-mode argmin over two identical Cayley factors. Zhang et al. 2020/21 examine equivalent multistep/single-step schemes. Layton et al. 2020 study variable-step DLN. Dharmaraja et al. 2009 use a trapezoidal-BDF split rather than two trapezoidal factors. A classical equivalent may be unindexed and one relevant old manuscript was not available for full reading.

value.rationale: Non-L-stable implicit midpoint/trapezoidal stepping has a recognized stiff-damping limitation. A constrained two-solve fixed-time allocation is a natural design problem. The theorem provides exact global optimizer with sharp zero/unequal/equal/unequal transitions for b<a/sqrt(3), a distinct equal/unequal transition above this angle, and a surviving nontrivial stiff-limit damping obtained by holding one substep near 2/sqrt(a²+b²). Not just a numerical tuning or known stability-region check; structural boundaries explain when equal subdivision can be suboptimal. No claims for accuracy, nonnormality or overall numerical efficiency.
